thread:
acme_prod_owner: Hey team — invoice #3491 shows ~240 reserved GPU hours charged for March but our token usage graph is flat for the same period. Can someone explain where the hours came from?

jamie_support: Sorry about that, tagging billing & infra. Can you paste the account id and the exact invoice line item?

acme_prod_owner: account: acct_ACME123, line: RESERVED_CAPACITY_CHARGE 2026-03. We saw a ~10x jump in "reserved hours" between 2026-03-12 02:00 -> 04:00 UTC but no traffic spike in our app logs.

maria_billing: Thanks. Pulling invoice, I see the line. Have you checked dedicated pool warmup or autoscale events? Those can consume commit hours (warmup instances count toward reserved).

acme_prod_owner: We didn't schedule any maintenance. Our dashboard for tokens (per-route) shows average 2k tokens/day during that window.

leo_infra: FYI deploy-bot shows a canary rollout at 2026-03-12T01:58:45Z on pool-id dp-42 in us-west1 which triggered 6 warmup instances. warmup tends to create GPU-backed instances that hit commit hours.

sophia_eng: Adding context: warmup behavior depends on pool config: `min_reserved_instances` + `warmup_strategy`. If warmup instances are not tagged/attributed correctly they can be billed to the customer's committed pool but not attributed to token metrics.

jamie_support: @acme_prod_owner can you confirm whether your Dedicated pool config has `enable_warmup: true` and if you have any custom hooks that hit the model after instance boot? Those calls show token burn but pure kernel warmup (LLM weight transfer) does not increase token counts.

acme_prod_owner: We do have warmup enabled. No post-boot inference calls from our side. So why 240 hours worth? That seems like multiple instances running for long time.

leo_infra: Looking at infra logs: dp-42 autoscaler performed repeated warmup cycles between 2026-03-12T01:58 and 2026-03-12T09:12. There was a bug where warmup retries didn't terminate on failed health-check, leaving instances alive for ~30–45m each. Instance ids: gpu-wn-1023, gpu-wn-1024, gpu-wn-1028.

maria_billing: Those instances are part of your committed pool and will be counted against reserved hours. We can apply a corrective SLA credit if the infra bug caused unintended burn. Please confirm you want us to apply an investigation credit and escalate to eng.

acme_prod_owner: Yes please. We need the credit and would like the root cause.

jamie_support: Next steps: 1) @leo_infra to collect instance lifetimes + healthcheck failures for those instance ids. 2) @sophia_eng to confirm whether warmup-retry bug was triggered and scope. 3) @maria_billing to tentatively open a credit case referencing invoice #3491 and hold the payment while we finish triage.

leo_infra: Copy. Exporting logs now. Quick snippet from kube events: 
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-12T02:03:10Z
Pod: gpu-wn-1023
Event: Readiness probe failed, retrying warmup (retry_count=3)
Action: probe loop continued (missing termination), created new warmup pod
```

sophia_eng: We pushed a fix for the warmup-retry state machine (PR: rwd/infra#6521) at 2026-03-12T10:05Z. It prevents warmup loops from leaving instances running. Seems to match your window.

maria_billing: For the credit request: please confirm affected hours estimate. leo, can you provide exact GPU-hour sum for acct_ACME123 during 2026-03-12 00:00 - 2026-03-13 00:00 UTC?

leo_infra: Preliminary tally: ~218.5 GPU-hours attributed to dp-42 that day. I'll attach per-instance breakdown in the incident ticket.

jamie_support: I'll open a support incident and link to the infra ticket + commit/PR. acme_prod_owner we'll follow up within 48h with a formal credit proposal. Sorry for the disruption :raised_hands:

acme_prod_owner: Thanks for the quick triage. For our side, is there a recommended mitigation so warmup doesn't count against reserved in future?

sophia_eng: Mitigations: - Set `max_warmup_retries: 0` to avoid retry loops - add a short post-boot smoke call that does 1 token inference to make attribution explicit (if you want charges attributed to on-demand instead) - or use `warmup: disabled` during maintenance windows. We'll draft recommended config snippets.

jamie_support: Action items recorded. I'll update the incident with the invoice hold and the requested infra dump.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rwd/infra#6521 merged by sophia_eng at 2026-03-12T10:05:21Z

maria_billing: Credit case opened: CASE-2026-ACME-78, pending infra confirmation.

acme_prod_owner: Appreciated. Will watch the incident.
